text: Lesson 13 left you with a clean list of normalized IOCs. The next question is what to actually do with them — and the naive answer, loop through them and query your SIEM once per indicator, falls apart fast. Against a feed with a few thousand IOCs, that's a few thousand round trips. This lesson builds one templated query instead, reusing the same Sentinel client you scripted against back in Chapter 2.

KQL's dynamic array, built inside a let statement, works like a parameterized IN clause. You join every IOC value into one array, drop it into a query against CommonSecurityLog filtered by a lookback window, and run that single query against the whole list at once instead of looping. One round trip, every indicator checked.

KQL queries do have a practical length ceiling, though, so a dynamic array built from tens of thousands of IOCs will blow past it. The fix is chunking: split the list into batches of a few thousand, run the same query once per batch using the LogsQueryClient you already know, and merge the results. The same discipline applies on the write side — bulk-updating a Sentinel watchlist in batches instead of hammering the API with thousands of single-item calls in a tight loop, which is exactly the kind of script a DevSecOps review would flag.

Once the matches come back, the real payoff is tagging. Pull every SourceIP and DestinationIP that matched into one set, then walk your normalized IOC list and mark each one seen in environment or not observed. That distinction matters enormously — an IOC merely sitting on a feed is informational, but an IOC that's on a feed and actually touched your logs is the one worth a human's attention.

That seen-in-environment tag isn't just a nice-to-have label — it's the signal the next lesson leans on hardest. Scoring and prioritizing threat intel means combining exactly this kind of real-world corroboration with a feed's raw confidence and how recently it was reported, so your team isn't drowning in alerts for indicators that never actually touched anything you run.
